business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company does not undertake in-house manufacturing of electrical equipment and does not own or operate any manufacturing facilities or significant plant and machinery; its operations are primarily contract-based. It procures electrical materials, equipment, consumables and spares required across its three service verticals from third-party manufacturers and suppliers on a project-specific basis, in accordance with project specifications, technical standards, tender conditions and contractual requirements. Materials procured typically include power and control cables, busbars, switchgear, circuit breakers, panels, protection and control systems, insulators, structural components and allied electrical accessories for the Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works vertical, and consumables, tools, spares and replacement components for the Network O&M and Metering verticals. Service verticals are executed through deployment of manpower, engagement of subcontractors, and use of tools and equipment at project sites. The Company does not maintain a centralised warehouse or centralised inventory facility; materials are generally delivered directly to project sites or stored at site-level facilities for the duration of the project, with inventory managed on a project-wise basis. Logistics operations are carried out through a combination of Company-owned vehicles (monitored through GPS-based systems) and third-party service providers. The Company intends to strengthen vendor and subcontractor networks and enhance project planning, procurement and inventory management systems.

overview.business_model: The Company sells field-execution services to electricity distribution utilities across three verticals: (i) Network Operation and Maintenance Services (maintenance and operational support of 33 kV, 11 kV and LT networks, O&M of 33/11 kV substations and deployment of technical manpower for line maintenance, network inspection and fault rectification), (ii) Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works (pole erection and shifting, laying/jointing/termination of underground and overhead cables and associated civil works such as excavation, foundations and plinths), and (iii) Metering and Meter Management Services (installation and replacement of energy meters, meter testing, meter reading and related field services). Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender processes conducted by electricity distribution utilities, pursuant to which the Company enters into rate contracts, outline agreements or annual maintenance contracts ("AMC") for defined service areas and contract periods, with specific purchase orders or work orders issued from time to time; for certain private sector clients works may be awarded directly through work orders or purchase orders without a formal tendering process. Execution involves deployment of field personnel (supervisors, linemen, technicians and helpers) supported by operational vehicles, tools and equipment. In Fiscal 2026, Network O&M Services contributed 76.90% of revenue from operations, Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works 14.66% and Metering and Meter Management Services 8.44%; by customer sector, electricity distribution utilities contributed 79.10%, integrated power utilities 9.04% and others 11.86%.

financial_valuation.detail: Operations require upfront deployment of resources and project expenses before customer receipts, with payments typically linked to milestones, inspections, certifications or completion stages and extended cycles due to administrative procedures of utilities. The Company relies on internal accruals, trade credit and working capital borrowings; delays in receivable realisation, inventory build-up or cost overruns may increase reliance on external borrowings and finance costs.
financial_valuation.evidence: Rs. in lakhs: Current Assets (excluding cash and cash equivalents) 5,947.22 (Fiscal 2026), 3,541.87 (Fiscal 2025), 3,208.83 (Fiscal 2024); Current Liabilities (excluding short-term borrowings) 2,219.41 / 1,672.57 / 1,821.54; Working Capital 3,727.81 / 1,869.30 / 1,387.29. Trade receivables Rs. 5,115.56 lakhs, Rs. 3,088.25 lakhs and Rs. 2,620.75 lakhs for Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively
financial_valuation.title: Working capital intensive business dependent on funding and receivable realisation

financial_valuation.detail: The Company has experienced negative cash flows from operating activities in certain financial periods, arising from increased working capital requirements, delays in customer receipts, capital expenditure or other operational requirements. Sustained negative cash flows may require reliance on external financing and may adversely affect liquidity and the ability to fund operations and growth plans.
financial_valuation.evidence: Net Cash Generated from Operating Activities (Rs. in lakhs): (330.99) Fiscal 2026, 108.18 Fiscal 2025, 38.67 Fiscal 2024
financial_valuation.title: Negative cash flows experienced in the past and may recur

financial_valuation.detail: Projects awarded through competitive bidding are executed on predetermined commercial terms and in certain cases are fixed-price or contain limited price escalation provisions. Increases in commodity prices, wage inflation, fuel costs, supply chain disruption and manpower availability may have to be absorbed, reducing operating margins, profitability and cash flows.
financial_valuation.title: Inability to pass on increases in labour, material, logistics and subcontracting costs

internal_operational.detail: The Company provides operation and maintenance and allied support services primarily to electricity distribution utilities in India, so demand is directly linked to utility capital expenditure, funding availability, government policy and schemes such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme. Any reduction or delay in utility capex, change in regulatory framework or constraint on utility investment capacity may reduce demand for services.
internal_operational.evidence: Sector-wise revenue (Rs. in lakhs): Electricity Distribution Utilities 12,372.19 / 79.10% (Fiscal 2026), 11,644.15 / 88.73% (Fiscal 2025), 9,935.52 / 88.87% (Fiscal 2024); Integrated Power Utilities 1,414.21 / 9.04%, 837.57 / 6.38%, 912.99 / 8.17%; Others 1,854.89 / 11.86%, 641.83 / 4.89%, 331.05 / 2.96%; Total Revenue from Operations 15,641.29 / 13,123.56 / 11,179.56
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentrated on power distribution utilities; reduction in business, adverse procurement changes or failure to secure new contracts

internal_operational.detail: A substantial portion of revenue from operations is derived from Network O&M Services. Reduction in scope of O&M activity, non-renewal or modification of service arrangements, changes in outsourcing policies of utilities, or a customer shift towards capex-driven projects or in-house execution may reduce the volume of work in this vertical.
internal_operational.evidence: Revenue by vertical (Rs. in lakhs): Network O&M Services 12,028.31 / 76.90% (FY 2025-26), 10,401.08 / 79.26% (FY 2024-25), 8,474.81 / 75.81% (FY 2023-24); Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works 2,293.10 / 14.66%, 1,006.46 / 7.67%, 1,513.08 / 13.53%; Metering and Meter Management Services 1,319.88 / 8.44%, 1,716.02 / 13.08%, 1,191.67 / 10.66%; Total 15,641.29 / 13,123.56 / 11,179.56
internal_operational.title: Substantial dependence on the Network Operation and Maintenance (O&M) service vertical

internal_operational.detail: Contracts are substantially secured through competitive tenders of electricity distribution utilities requiring prescribed technical qualifications, financial eligibility, prior experience, manpower availability and statutory registrations, which may become more stringent over time. Competitive bidding may limit the ability to maintain or improve operating margins. The Company confirms there have been no past instances of disqualification from tenders or inability to execute awarded contracts for failure to meet eligibility criteria.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on competitive tendering processes and ability to meet eligibility criteria and competitive pricing

strategy_growth.detail: The electrical infrastructure services industry comprises various contractors and service providers, and certain competitors may have longer operating histories, larger scale, greater financial resources, broader service offerings or more established utility relationships. Competition is based on technical qualifications, execution track record, pricing, manpower availability and ability to meet tender requirements, and competitive intensity in tenders may push pricing and margins down, potentially resulting in reduced order inflows or loss of market share.
strategy_growth.evidence: Competitors include Rajesh Power Services Limited and Parth Electricals & Engineering Private Limited, among others
strategy_growth.title: Competitive industry with established and regional competitors

strategy_growth.detail: Customers may adopt new technologies, equipment standards, digital monitoring systems, smart grid technologies, advanced metering infrastructure and automation-based solutions, and tender qualification criteria and specifications may change. Inability to monitor developments, upgrade technical capabilities, train and retain skilled manpower or adapt operational processes may hinder qualification for tenders and execution to evolving standards, while adopting new technologies may require additional investment in training, equipment, tools or systems.
strategy_growth.title: Failure to identify and adapt to evolving industry trends, technological developments and customer requirements

strategy_growth.detail: Industry-related information in the Red Herring Prospectus is derived from a report commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the purpose of the Offer. The report is based on secondary statistics, assumptions and parameters, does not purport to be exhaustive, and has not been independently verified by the Company, the BRLM or their affiliates; there are no standard data-gathering methodologies in the industry, and investors should not place undue reliance on such information.
strategy_growth.evidence: Industry report titled Global and Indian Power EPC Industry issued on February 17, 2026 (the Infomerics Report), prepared by Infomerics Analytics & Research Private Limited, commissioned vide engagement letter dated January 22, 2026; the Company, its Promoters and Directors are not related to Infomerics Analytics & Research Private Limited
strategy_growth.title: Reliance on an industry report commissioned and paid for by the Company

concerns_observed: FY26 cash flow from operations was negative ₹(330.99) lakhs against PAT of ₹1,046.57 lakhs; cumulative three-year CFO is ₹(184.14) lakhs against cumulative PAT of ₹1,792.97 lakhs — reported profit has not converted to operating cash in any of the three years.

Trade receivables of ₹5,115.56 lakhs are 32.7% of FY26 revenue (roughly 119 days) versus 23.5% (86 days) in FY25 and 23.4% (86 days) in FY24; receivables grew 65.6% against revenue growth of 19.2%, an increase of ₹2,027.31 lakhs in one year.

Extreme concentration on every axis in FY26: Odisha 69.05% of revenue, top-10 customers 94.76%, largest single customer ₹5,212.95 lakhs / 33.33%, top-3 customers 64.79%, Network O&M vertical 76.90%, and electricity distribution utilities 79.10%.

Of ₹2,800 lakhs of quantified objects, ₹2,200 lakhs (78.6%) funds working capital and ₹600 lakhs repays the ₹1,394.47 lakh Bank of Maharashtra cash credit — no object adds capacity or capability; the general corporate purposes amount is ₹[•].

The entire margin step-up is one year old: EBITDA margin roughly doubled from 6.13% to 10.90% in FY26 while the extraction records no one-off items and no working-capital days table, leaving the step-up undecomposed.

Contingent liabilities of ₹872.35 lakhs equal 25.91% of networth (FY25 ₹494.55 lakhs, FY24 nil), of which ₹828.36 lakhs is outstanding bank guarantees furnished to utilities — up from ₹458.94 lakhs a year earlier.
The FY26 receivables build was financed by short-term borrowing: financing inflows included ₹784.68 lakhs of short-term borrowings against a ₹(543.08) lakh investing outflow and negative CFO.

The DRHP itself states the order book comprises rate contracts, service-level arrangements and maintenance contracts that do not assure any minimum quantum of work, with execution dependent on utility work orders and budget allocations.
Haryana revenue fell from ₹922.69 lakhs (8.25%) in FY24 to ₹6.42 lakhs (0.05%) in FY25 and nil in FY26 — a precedent for non-continuity in a state the company had highlighted as a milestone win.

Contracts are won on competitive tender at predetermined, in certain cases fixed-price, terms with limited escalation, against a labour-intensive cost base of 4,473 personnel as on May 31, 2026 (4,295 deployed in operations).
A significant portion of existing bank borrowings is secured by personal guarantees of directors Jawed Akhtar and Sunil Lakshman Vatsa, which may continue post listing.

The Red Herring Prospectus will not be filed with SEBI and SEBI will not issue observations on the Offer Document (Regulation 246(2) of SEBI ICDR); filing is with BSE Limited only, and no monitoring agency is appointed as the offer excluding OFS is below ₹5,000 lakh.
data_gaps: Offer price and price band are ₹[•] throughout, so no valuation multiple can be computed against the stated peer set (industry P/E high 39.20, low 10.69, average 24.95) or against FY26 EPS of ₹12.64 and NAV of ₹40.66.

Promoters' average cost of acquisition per share is not stated — all three entries (Jawed Akhtar, Sunil Lakshman Vatsa, Furquan Akhtar) are null, despite a risk factor that it may be lower than the offer price.
Dilution percentage, total project cost and the objects funding mix (fresh issue / debt / internal accrual) are all null; the general corporate purposes amount is ₹[•] in both implementation years.
Trade payables are absent from all three balance-sheet years, so the cash conversion cycle cannot be closed; the working-capital days table is empty.
Trade receivables ageing beyond one year is not disclosed (gt_1yr_amount_lakhs null), so the quality of the ₹5,115.56 lakh receivable book cannot be assessed.
Lock-in disclosure is truncated — no expiry dates for the promoters' 20% contribution, no promoter-excess lock-in period, no lock-in on other pre-issue capital, and no anchor-investor lock-in terms.
One-off items are recorded as none and no cost bridge is available, so the FY26 EBITDA margin step-up from 6.13% to 10.90% cannot be decomposed.
Top-5 customer concentration and top-1 supplier concentration are not given (only top-1/top-10 for customers and top-5/top-10 for suppliers).
Market position is empty — no market share, positioning statement or basis; the SWOT carries four strengths and no weaknesses, opportunities or threats.
Group companies, the past non-compliances table and KMP attrition are all empty in the extraction, so prior-entity and management-churn history cannot be assessed.
Employee strength in the overview is null; the only headcount available is 4,473 (4,295 deployed) as on May 31, 2026, taken from a risk factor.

Every milestone year in the corporate genesis timeline is blank, so the approximately ₹200 crore eastern-India contract, the approximately ₹150 crore FRT contract and the Middle East EPC assignment cannot be dated or sequenced.

Only two peers are given (Rajesh Power Services Limited and Parth Electricals & Engineering Limited), both FY2026 and neither scale-matched — Rajesh Power's total income of ₹1,63,341.29 lakhs is over ten times the Company's ₹15,641.29 lakhs; peer symbols are blank and no global comparables are provided.
Litigation counts by party are null (only amounts: ₹78.21 lakhs company, ₹3.42 lakhs promoters/directors), and 'actions by statutory and regulatory authorities' is stated as 'Not ascertainable'.
Board committee disclosure covers only the Audit Committee — no Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship or other committee composition is captured.

Only one KMP predates the offer window (Company Secretary Aarti Garg, since 01.05.2025); the CEO and CFO both date from 01.05.2026, so there is no management tenure record across the restated financial period.
The GST returns delay table is extracted with delay-day and amount columns not separable (2023-24 1290.43; 2024-25 1964.48; 2025-26 2260.23), so GST delay magnitude cannot be read reliably.
Order book unexecuted percentage is null and no execution schedule by year is given for the ₹553.70 crore book.

Capacity, utilisation and post-expansion metrics are all null — the business is contract and manpower based with no plants or capacity data, so no throughput-based check on the growth plan is possible.
monitorables: Quarterly trade receivables and operating cash flow — whether the FY26 CFO of ₹(330.99) lakhs reverses once the ₹2,200 lakhs of working-capital proceeds are deployed, or whether receivable days stay near the FY26 level of about 119.
Durability of the FY26 EBITDA margin of 10.90% against the FY24-FY25 band of 5.49-6.13%.
Conversion of the ₹553.70 crore / 34-project order book at June 30, 2026 into billed revenue, and the rate of fresh tender wins from electricity distribution utilities.
Odisha's share of revenue (69.05% in FY26, 74.52% FY25) and whether Maharashtra (12.45%) and the newly entered Gujarat (6.63%) scale enough to reduce single-state dependence.
Top-10 customer share (94.76% FY26) and whether the largest customer's 33.33% share is renewed on comparable terms.
Renewal of the Odisha electrical contractor license (valid to August 15, 2026) and grant of the pending fresh MV/HT/EHT category license, plus contract labour licenses expiring through Fiscal 2027.
Timeliness of PF, ESIC, PT, TDS and GST remittances from FY2026-27 onward, given delays persisted to March 2026.

Completion of name-change amendments across electrical contractor licenses, GST registrations, EPF/ESIC records, trademark applications (Classes 35, 36, 37, 39), the Berhampur trade license and insurance policies.
Outstanding bank guarantees (₹828.36 lakhs at March 31, 2026, up from ₹458.94 lakhs) and any invocation by utilities.
Whether the ₹1,394.47 lakh Bank of Maharashtra cash credit falls by the ₹600 lakhs applied from proceeds, or short-term borrowings re-expand (they rose ₹784.68 lakhs in FY26).
Any further promoter or promoter-group sales beyond the 3,60,000 shares sold to Convivial Advisors LLP, and creation of the three-year lock-in on 20% of post-issue capital.
Audit Committee disclosures on utilisation of net proceeds, since no monitoring agency has been appointed.
Closure or dropping orders for the GST proceedings where demands were paid — ₹11.12 lakhs (FY2020-21) and ₹2.86 lakhs (FY2021-22), Mumbai — and the ₹76.90 lakh indirect-tax exposure.
Contingent liabilities trend after ₹872.35 lakhs (25.91% of networth) in FY26 versus ₹494.55 lakhs FY25 and nil FY24.
Retention and cost of the 4,473-person workforce (4,295 deployed as on May 31, 2026) against fixed-rate and limited-escalation tender contracts.
Whether the three service verticals rebalance further, after Metering fell to 8.44% of FY26 revenue from 13.08% and Electrical Infrastructure rose to 14.66% from 7.67%.
open_questions: What drove EBITDA margin from 6.13% in FY25 to 10.90% in FY26 — contract mix, rate revisions, or cost timing — given no one-off items are recorded and the Electrical Infrastructure vertical rose from 7.67% to 14.66% of revenue in the same year?

What reconciles the ₹5,14,32,816 difference between audited Reserves and Surplus of ₹28,29,46,189 and restated ₹23,15,13,373 at March 31, 2025, and which of the two supported the 200:1 bonus capitalisation of January 15, 2026?
Why did trade receivables rise 65.6% to ₹5,115.56 lakhs against 19.2% revenue growth, and what portion is outstanding beyond one year (ageing not disclosed)?

In the related-party table Jawed Akhtar's director-loan balance moves from an FY2025 opening of ₹353.74 lakhs to an FY2025 closing of ₹1.02 lakhs while FY2025 flows show ₹483.98 lakhs received and ₹131.26 lakhs repaid — what reconciles the stated flows to the stated balances?

Why did both promoters each sell 1,80,000 shares (2.17%) to Convivial Advisors LLP on July 20 and 21, 2026, days before the RHP, and at what price — and what is Convivial Advisors LLP's relationship to the promoters?

Does the stated post-offer promoter holding of 70,34,790 shares (62.37%) net the 2,50,000 shares being sold in the Offer for Sale, or would post-OFS promoter holding be 67,84,790 shares (60.15%) of the 1,12,79,190 post-offer shares?
How much of the ₹553.70 crore order book is under fixed-rate terms with no price escalation, and over what period is it expected to be executed?
Why is Haryana revenue nil in FY26 after ₹922.69 lakhs (8.25%) in FY24 — contract completion, non-renewal, or loss on retender?

What receivable-days assumption underlies the ₹2,200 lakhs working-capital requirement for FY2026-27 and the period to September 30, 2027, and what is the shortfall if realisation stays at FY26 levels?
Why did PF, ESIC, PT and TDS remittance delays persist through January-March 2026 after the monitoring system and maker-checker controls were stated to have been implemented?
What are the identities, contract tenures and renewal dates of Customers 1, 2 and 3 (₹5,212.95, ₹2,687.47 and ₹2,233.04 lakhs in FY26 — 64.79% of revenue combined)?
Which director-owned premises are leased to the Company, on what rentals, and are those rentals captured in the related-party table (which shows only remuneration, salary and loans)?
Given both the CEO and CFO were appointed on 01.05.2026, who held those functions during the FY2024-FY2026 period covered by the restated financial statements?
verdict.our_read: A power-distribution O&M contractor (FY26 revenue ₹15,641.29 lakhs, EBITDA margin 10.90%, order book ₹553.70 crore) whose thesis rides on converting Odisha-concentrated utility receivables of ₹5,115.56 lakhs into cash — FY26 operating cash flow was ₹(330.99) lakhs.

parameter_scores.basis: CFO ₹(330.99) lakhs in FY26 against PAT ₹1,046.57 lakhs; three-year cumulative CFO ₹(184.14) lakhs against cumulative PAT ₹1,792.97 lakhs; receivables increased ₹2,027.31 lakhs and inventory ₹220.87 lakhs in FY26.

FY26: Odisha 69.05%, top-10 customers 94.76% (₹14,822.04 lakhs), top-1 customer 33.33% (₹5,212.95 lakhs), Network O&M vertical 76.90%, electricity distribution utilities 79.10%; Haryana went from 8.25% (FY24) to nil.

FY2025-26 PF delays of ₹911.39 lakhs (1-214 days) and ESIC ₹123.40 lakhs (1-148 days), continuing into January-March 2026; Form 2 for the 4,000-share allotment and pre-2012 transfer records untraceable (GNL-1 SRN AC3427275); MGT-14s for 2014/2021/2025 resolutions and CSR-2 for FY2022-23 and FY2023-24 filed only in February-March 2026; CHG-1 never filed for the Mahindra Finance charge.

Reserves and Surplus at March 31, 2025 stated as ₹28,29,46,189 (audited) versus ₹23,15,13,373 (restated), a ₹5,14,32,816 gap; a risk factor states promoters and promoter group will hold 100% post-offer against the stated 62.37%; offer price is ₹[•] and promoters' average cost of acquisition is not stated.

Board of 5 with 2 independent directors and only the Audit Committee disclosed, on which promoter and Chairman Jawed Akhtar sits; promoters, promoter group and directors hold 95.65% pre-offer; promoter Furquan Akhtar (age 22, 1 year stated experience) appointed CEO on 01.05.2026 and CFO Dharmendra Shahi appointed the same date; no promoter or executive director has listed-company experience.

₹2,200 lakhs of ₹2,800 lakhs quantified objects to working capital, ₹600 lakhs to repaying the ₹1,394.47 lakh cash credit, none to capacity; fund requirement based on management estimates, not appraised by any bank, financial institution or agency; no monitoring agency; 200:1 bonus of 82,38,000 shares on January 15, 2026, four months before the offer.
parameter_scores.parameter: Use of proceeds and offer structure

parameter_scores.basis: ₹553.70 crore unexecuted across 34 projects at June 30, 2026, roughly 3.5x FY26 revenue of ₹15,641.29 lakhs, but stated to consist of rate contracts and AMCs with no assured minimum quantum; repeat customers 88.29% of FY26 revenue.

EBITDA margin 5.49% → 6.13% → 10.90% and PAT margin 2.51% → 3.55% → 6.69% across FY24-FY26; the entire step-up sits in FY26 with no one-off items recorded and no working-capital or cost-bridge disclosure to decompose it.

Total debt ₹1,647.13 lakhs on networth ₹3,366.56 lakhs (0.49x) with cash ₹601.33 lakhs; indebtedness ₹1,635.51 lakhs as on May 31, 2026 dominated by a ₹1,394.47 lakh cash credit at 9.05%; contingent liabilities ₹872.35 lakhs equal 25.91% of networth.

RoNW 31.09% / RoCE 31.13% / RoE 36.81% in FY26 versus 20.09% / 23.88% / 23.16% in FY25 and 16.44% / 27.14% / 17.91% in FY24, on net fixed assets of ₹580.29 lakhs and nil CWIP — but earned on a networth base of only ₹3,366.56 lakhs and not backed by operating cash.
Revenue ₹11,179.56 → ₹13,123.56 → ₹15,641.29 lakhs (+17.4%, +19.2%); PAT more than doubled in FY26 to ₹1,046.57 lakhs; order book of ₹553.70 crore at June 30, 2026 is about 3.5x FY26 revenue.

Aggregate litigation ₹81.63 lakhs — ₹78.21 lakhs against the Company (direct tax ₹1.31 lakhs, indirect tax ₹76.90 lakhs) and ₹3.42 lakhs against promoters/directors — equal to 7.8% of FY26 PAT and 2.42% of networth; nil criminal proceedings; four labour matters; actions by statutory and regulatory authorities stated as 'Not ascertainable'.

red_flags: Reserves and Surplus at March 31, 2025 differ by ₹5,14,32,816 between the audited financial statements (₹28,29,46,189) and the Restated Financial Statements (₹23,15,13,373) — the reserve pool from which 82,38,000 bonus shares were capitalised on January 15, 2026; a bonus-issue certificate from M/s SSKN & Associates dated March 27, 2026 was obtained.

Chronic and worsening statutory-dues delays: FY2025-26 PF ₹911.39 lakhs delayed 1-214 days (up from ₹413.51 lakhs in FY2023-24), ESIC ₹123.40 lakhs delayed 1-148 days, PT ₹31.95 lakhs and TDS other than salary ₹12.31 lakhs — with delays continuing during January to March 2026 despite stated remedial controls.

Both promoters sold 1,80,000 shares each (2.17% each) to Convivial Advisors LLP on July 20 and 21, 2026, within six months of the RHP; Convivial Advisors LLP is now the only public shareholder holding 1% or more, at 3,60,000 shares (4.35%).

Untraceable historical corporate records: the Form 2 return of allotment for 4,000 equity shares, 1985 incorporation forms, pre-2012 share transfer records and the bank statements evidencing consideration for the 1,981 and 2,000 share transfers that brought in the current promoters; GNL-1 filed vide SRN AC3427275; search report by M/s. Neeraj Jain and Associates dated February 19, 2026.

Bonus issue of 82,38,000 shares in a 200:1 ratio on January 15, 2026 on a pre-bonus base of only 41,190 shares (itself created by a May 27, 2025 sub-division), lifting pre-offer capital to 82,79,190 shares four months before the offer and leaving the Securities Premium Account nil.

A cluster of ROC filing defaults cured only months before the offer: MGT-14 for a February 2014 resolution filed March 26, 2026; MGT-14s for September and October 2021 resolutions filed February 14, 2026; CSR-2 for FY2022-23 and FY2023-24 both filed March 26, 2026; CHG-1 never filed for the Mahindra Finance Services charge; clerical and typographical inaccuracies in Forms AOC-4 and MGT-7 that cannot be rectified by revision.

The company's own risk factor states 'The promoter along with the promoter group will continue to hold collectively 100% of the Equity share capital of the company', which contradicts the stated pre-offer holding of 95.65% (Convivial Advisors LLP holds 4.35% publicly) and the stated post-offer promoter holding of 62.37%.

Promoter Furquan Akhtar, aged 22 with 1 year of stated experience, was appointed Chief Executive Officer on 01.05.2026; the Chief Financial Officer was appointed the same day; none of the promoters or executive directors has experience managing a listed company.

Inter-promoter transfer of 3,20,595 shares (3.87%) from Jawed Akhtar to Sunil Lakshman Vatsa on March 25, 2026, equalising both at 34,36,995 shares (41.51%) each, in the same window as the offer authorisations (Board March 02, 2026; EGM March 03, 2026).
CSR spending obligation under Section 135 for Fiscal 2023 was not met within the prescribed timeline and was remitted only subsequently.

Three employee accident insurance policies covering 240, 350 and 175 employees respectively have expired with renewed schedules only awaited, and several policies, licenses, GST registrations and trademarks still stand in the erstwhile name G V Electricals Private Limited.

Registered office, area offices, warehouses and guest houses are largely on 10 or 11 month leave-and-license tenures, some from lessors who are directors of the Company; 14 of 18 premises are not owned.
strengths_observed: Order book of ₹553.70 crore across 34 ongoing projects as of June 30, 2026 — about 3.5x FY26 revenue from operations of ₹15,641.29 lakhs.
EBITDA margin expanded 5.49% (FY24) to 6.13% (FY25) to 10.90% (FY26), with PAT rising ₹280.32 → ₹466.08 → ₹1,046.57 lakhs and restated EPS ₹3.47 → ₹5.77 → ₹12.64.

RoNW 31.09% and RoCE 31.13% in FY26 (20.09%/23.88% FY25, 16.44%/27.14% FY24) on an asset-light base — net fixed assets of only ₹580.29 lakhs against ₹15,641.29 lakhs of revenue, with no owned manufacturing facilities.
Repeat customers contributed ₹13,809.21 lakhs, 88.29% of FY26 revenue (97.14% in FY25, 99.28% in FY24), under rate contracts and AMCs with electricity distribution utilities.
Revenue grew 17.4% in FY25 and 19.2% in FY26, from ₹11,179.56 lakhs to ₹15,641.29 lakhs over three years.
Debt-to-networth of 0.49x at March 31, 2026 (total debt ₹1,647.13 lakhs against networth ₹3,366.56 lakhs), cash of ₹601.33 lakhs, and no promoter shares pledged or otherwise encumbered.

Vertical and geographic broadening within FY26: Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works rose to ₹2,293.10 lakhs (14.66%) from ₹1,006.46 lakhs (7.67%), and Gujarat entered at ₹1,036.40 lakhs (6.63%) from ₹7.57 lakhs (0.06%).
Supplier concentration eased sharply — top-5 purchases fell to 29.05% of total purchases in FY26 from 57.31% in FY25; top-10 to 46.79% from 70.50%.
Working capital (current assets ex-cash less current liabilities ex-short-term borrowings) of ₹3,727.81 lakhs at FY26 against ₹1,869.30 lakhs at FY25, and NAV per share of ₹40.66 at March 31, 2026.
